analysis.reasoning:
(a) CONTAINER TYPE: `previous_stages_out` is always a LIST, never a dict. It is created as `[None] * num_frames` in `_construct_initial_input_batch` (OLD SCSam3VideoInference.py:164; OLD NewMem:165; NEW:164/:170), which `init_state` calls unconditionally at OLD SCSam3VideoInference.py:77 (`self._construct_initial_input_batch(inference_state, images)`). The ONLY construction path for an inference_state reaching the change sites is `SCSam3VideoPredictor{,NewMem}.start_session` -> `self.model.init_state(...)` (demoSCSam3MVOpt/SCSam3VideoPredictorNewMem.py:120, SCSam3VideoPredictor.py:119). The change sites live in `add_tracker_new_points` (def at :1425) and `add_tracker_new_mask` (def at :1681), reachable only through `add_prompt` (:1391, :1405), which is dispatched on that same session state. So the key is ALWAYS present and ALWAYS bound to a list of length num_frames before these lines run.

(c) THE REMOVED GUARDS WERE BOTH DEAD, AND WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG IF LIVE. Guard 1 `if "previous_stages_out" not in inference_state` is never true (key set at :164 before any prompt). Guard 2 `if frame_idx not in inference_state["previous_stages_out"]` is applied to a LIST, so `in` is VALUE membership, not index membership: the list only ever holds None, the string "_THIS_FRAME_HAS_OUTPUTS_", or `out` dicts, and an int `frame_idx` never compares equal to any of those. I verified this by simulation: for every frame_idx 0..N-1, against both a fresh `[None]*N` and a list already containing the sentinel and a prior `out` dict, `frame_idx not in list` is True in all cases. Therefore the first branch (`[frame_idx] = out`, an ordinary list index assignment) was ALWAYS taken and the `.update(out)` merge branch was UNREACHABLE. Moreover, had guard 1 ever fired and swapped the list for a dict, it would have BROKEN the downstream readers: `all(out is None for out in previous_stages_out)` iterates dict KEYS (ints), yielding False, and `enumerate(previous_stages_out)` on a dict yields (position, key) rather than (index, value) — so `min(t ...)` would return an enumeration position, not a frame index. The removed code was not a safety net; it was a latent hazard that never triggered.

(b) EVERY READ, exhaustively (grep for `previous_stages_out` over both packages, upstream sam3, and runMVSeg.py; nothing else in the repo touches it):
  - reset_state, OLD/NEW SCSam3VideoInference.py:97 (NewMem:98/:103): `[t] = None` — a WRITE (index assignment, requires a list; would have raised on OLD's hypothetical dict).
  - `_get_visual_prompt`, :188 (NewMem:189/:194): `... is None` only. Feeds `is_new_visual_prompt`. Both a dict and the string are non-None, so identical.
  - `_get_processing_order`, :225 (NewMem:226/:231): `all(out is None for out in previous_stages_out)` — is-None only.
  - `_get_processing_order`, :233 (NewMem:234/:239): `min(t for t, out in enumerate(previous_stages_out) if out is not None)` — is-not-None only; the VALUE is discarded, only the index `t` is used.
  - `_run_single_frame_inference`, :398 (NewMem:400/:405): a WRITE of the same sentinel string, present identically in OLD, NEW and upstream.
  - Upstream sam3/sam3/model/sam3_video_inference.py: :99 (write None), :166 (list init), :190 (is None), :227 (is None), :235 (is not None), :400 (sentinel write). Identical set.
  - sam3/sam3/model/sam3_image.py:537/572/573 uses a same-named LOCAL variable (a SAM3Output), completely unrelated to the inference_state key.
  - No other reader anywhere: not in SCSam3TrackerPredictor*.py, SCSam3Video.py, SCSam3VideoPredictor*.py, io_utils.py, or runMVSeg.py. No consumer indexes into the value, no truthiness test, no `.get`, no serialization (no torch.save/pickle/deepcopy/json.dump anywhere in either package) that would embed the value.
  CONCLUSION: zero readers consume the value beyond an is-None / is-not-None test. Since `out` is a 3-key dict (always truthy, always non-None) and "_THIS_FRAME_HAS_OUTPUTS_" is likewise non-None, every reader observes the identical result on every frame.

(d) UPSTREAM: yes, upstream SAM 3 uses exactly this sentinel, at sam3/sam3/model/sam3_video_inference.py:400, with the same comment ("use a dummy string in 'previous_stages_out' to indicate this frame has outputs"). Note further that upstream's `add_tracker_new_points` does NOT write previous_stages_out at all — its rank-0 block (sam3_video_inference.py:1580-1610) builds `out`, calls `_cache_frame_outputs`, and returns. The write at these four sites is the author's local "최종 패치", added so `_get_processing_order` can find a start frame after an interactive prompt. NEW preserves that marking semantics exactly while switching the stored value to upstream's own sentinel form. Additionally, three sibling packages in this same repo already carry the identical sentinel form at the identical line numbers — demoSCSam3OneStage/SCSam3VideoInference.py:1661 and :1912, demoSCSam3TwoStage/SCSam3VideoInference.py:1661 and :1912, demoSCSam3TwoStageNew/SCSam3VideoInference.py:1661 and :1912 — so this exact edit is prior art in the codebase, not a novel deviation.

NET EFFECT: on every reachable call path, OLD executed `previous_stages_out[frame_idx] = out` and NEW executes `previous_stages_out[frame_idx] = "_THIS_FRAME_HAS_OUTPUTS_"`. Both write a non-None value at the same list index; no reader distinguishes them. The local `out` variable is untouched and still flows to `_postprocess_output(...)` and the return value at :1918-1920, so the caller-visible result is byte-identical. The only difference is that OLD's stored dict kept `obj_id_to_mask` (video-resolution masks) and an alias of `tracker_metadata["obj_id_to_score"]` alive for the whole session; NEW drops that reference. Both NEW files compile cleanly. For this change site, the user's belief holds.

results.title: RetireSpatialPredictor method and uses_spatial_predictor flag added to SCSam3Video.py

analysis.reasoning:
SCSam3Video.py differs between the two packages ONLY by the two additions under test (verified by direct diff: OLD has no flag and no method; the file is otherwise byte-identical).

(a) The runner's behavior DOES change, but its request shapes do not.
 - Dead code becomes live: runMVSeg.py:335 `if hasattr(sc, "RetireSpatialPredictor")` is False for OLD, so today the OneStageNew run never retires anything and never calls `torch.clear_autocast_cache()` (runMVSeg.py:336-338). After the copy that block executes on every OneStageNew run. So "copying NEW over OLD changes nothing the runner does" is false at the process level: ~3.2 GiB of parameters plus the cross-view session are dropped mid-run, and a global autocast-cache clear happens. That is the intended memory win, not an accident.
 - Propagate request shape is unchanged. runMVSeg.py:251-252 reads `getattr(self, "uses_spatial_predictor", getattr(self, "predictor_spatial", None) is not None)`. OLD: no flag, `predictor_spatial` is a live object (never retired) -> fallback True -> multi-session branch (`session_ids` + `spatial_idx`, runMVSeg.py:253-254). NEW: flag is literally True (SCSam3Video.py:23) -> same branch. Identical request in both. Track-camera selection is also identical: runMVSeg.py:46 lists both algos in NEEDS_ALL_VIEWS, so track_mode is "all" either way (runMVSeg.py:304).
 - The flag is load-bearing, not cosmetic. After retire, `predictor_spatial` is None, so the OLD fallback expression would evaluate False and the runner would send `session_id` instead of `session_ids`; SCSam3VideoPredictorNewMem.handle_stream_request does `session_ids=request["session_ids"]` unconditionally (SCSam3VideoPredictorNewMem.py:100), i.e. an immediate KeyError. Flag and method must travel together.

(b) On the runner's reachable path, nothing touches predictor_spatial after retire. main() is straight-line: LoadCameraFolders (309), AddReferenceMask (318), PropagateAcrossViews (321), retire (335-336), TrackForward (340), write loop (342-356). The only uses of the cross-view predictor are through the `spatial` property (runMVSeg.py:144) at lines 180, 184, 190 and 210 - all before 335 - and TrackForward/the write loop run purely on `self.predictor` (runMVSeg.py:230, 257). No exception handler re-enters a spatial call. Retire is idempotent (MVOpt/SCSam3Video.py:52-54).
 BUT the guard is a docstring claim that is factually wrong, and it leaves a real trap. MVOpt/SCSam3Video.py:46-48 says the attribute is set to None "rather than deleted so that an older caller sniffing hasattr(...) still takes the multi-session branch". hasattr does stay True, but the runner does not use hasattr for that - it uses `getattr(self, "predictor_spatial", self.predictor)` (runMVSeg.py:144), and getattr's default only fires when the attribute is MISSING. With the attribute present and None, `self.spatial` returns None, not the `self.predictor` fallback (verified with a Python repro). `del self.predictor_spatial` would have made that fallback work; `= None` guarantees an AttributeError on NoneType instead. Every base-class method that uses the predictor directly is likewise now a post-retire landmine: MVOpt/SCSam3Video.py:79-80, 90-91, 140/149 (LoadVideo_File), 172 (AddPoint), 186 (AddText), 216 (InitializeSegmentation). None is on today's path; all are newly fragile.

(c) masks_spatial is fully materialized host data and cannot be affected by retiring. `_postprocess_output` returns `"out_binary_masks": out_binary_masks.cpu().numpy()` (SCSam3VideoInference.py:517) - a host numpy array, itself built from torch.cat/index_select temporaries (459, 486), not a view into inference_state. runMVSeg.py:214 then does `out["out_binary_masks"][i] > 0.0`, which allocates a fresh numpy bool array. TrackForward re-materializes again with `torch.tensor(mask, dtype=torch.float32)` (runMVSeg.py:234). No GPU residency, no aliasing to the session or the model; the MVOpt copy does not touch _postprocess_output (its hunks are at 1653/1877/1902). The cross-view generator is fully drained by the for-loop at runMVSeg.py:211 before retire, so no suspended generator holds session state.

(d) No numerical channel that I can find. The two predictors are independent objects with independent models (build_scsam3.py:994-1001; each builder constructs its own backbone/text encoder/transformer at 740-748 vs 880-888) and, critically, independent class-level session registries (SCSam3VideoPredictor.py:26 vs SCSam3VideoPredictorNewMem.py:24,26), so closing the cross-view session cannot touch the temporal sessions the tracker reads (SCSam3VideoPredictorNewMem.py:202-204). Retire consumes no RNG: the only torch.randn in the package is the compile warm-up (SCSam3VideoInference.py:721-731), which is gated on compile=True (default False, SCSam3VideoPredictor.py:38) and runs at build time anyway; gc.collect/empty_cache/dict.pop do not advance any generator. The autocast concern resolves benignly: the tracker enters `torch.autocast` at construction and never exits (SCSam3TrackerPredictor.py:51-52 and NewMem:51-52), so dropping the retired model's context object without `__exit__` leaves the thread-local nesting exactly as it already was; `torch.clear_autocast_cache()` only drops cached `param.to(bf16)` results, which recompute bit-identically (fp32->bf16 round-to-nearest-even is deterministic on unchanged weights). No __del__ anywhere in the predictor modules, so dropping the reference does not run shutdown(), does not destroy the NCCL group (SCSam3VideoPredictor.py:519) and does not stop workers; and this box has one GPU (nvidia-smi -L), so world_size==1 - no barrier, no worker dispatch, no collective involved in close_session.
 The one residual channel is indirect: freeing ~3.2 GiB and calling empty_cache changes allocator state and free-memory-dependent kernel/workspace heuristics under PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments (runMVSeg.py:33). cudnn.benchmark is never enabled in this repo (only train/trainer.py:273, unused at inference), so this is weak, but it is the only way a written PNG could differ, and only for logits within an ulp of the 0.0 threshold.

(e) It is a memory fix in effect and a new public API in form - both, not either. The saving is real and the outputs are unchanged on the runner's path; but the class grows a public method and a public flag, the runner's OneStageNew path executes new code it never executed for the published numbers, and the object acquires a one-shot lifecycle (post-retire it can no longer do a second cross-view pass, which OLD supported). "Only memory bug-fixes with zero behavioral change" is not an accurate description of this site; "output-equivalent memory fix that adds new API and a new object lifecycle" is.
